population.note: FICTIONAL. US adults are about 276M. Current users: 35.7% ≈ 98.5M. Ever used: 48.5% ≈ 133.9M, up 8.5 pts (limit 10.2). Off now: 48.5 − 35.7 = 12.8 pts ≈ 35.3M. Never used: ≈142M. Cycling: about 18.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.0 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (18.0 + 5.0)/48.5 ≈ 47.4%. That is consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Drug holidays prompted by the anhedonia label count as adherence breaks, not stops, unless they last more than 90 days. Age check: 18–29: 22% × 51M = 11.2M; 30–49: 40% × 92M = 36.8M; 50–64: 50.5% × 62M = 31.3M; 65+: 27% × 71M = 19.2M. Total 98.5M. Income thirds average (39 + 35.5 + 32.6)/3 = 35.7. Top-third growth comes from the retatrutide autoinjector and coached regimens. Middle-third growth is mostly cash portal buyers pushed off employer plans. Bottom-third growth comes from Medicaid (11.5M→15.0M users) and imports (7.1M→8.4M). The 65+ band rose 21→27%, driven by retatrutide's Part D listing and partly offset by bone pauses and post-NAION stops. The off-now 35.3M are concentrated among people whose employer coverage ended in 2035–36 and who could not carry the $199–279 portal price, plus long-term pausers. The never-used are skewed toward under-30s, where the Unmedicated movement is a cause as well as a description, along with rural non-expansion states and people with contraindications. Pediatric: 1.5% of ≈73M ≈ 1.1M, of whom ≈120k are aged 6–11 since the Oct 2035 liraglutide approval, mostly on generic liraglutide through Medicaid EPSDT. Roughly half of US children now live with at least one parent who is on the drug, cycling or on holiday.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Part D obesity benefit statute unchanged: $199/month negotiated rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 plus a comorbidity. Retatrutide (12 mg autoinjector) was added to Part D formularies at the statutory rate in Sep 2035 under a CMS–Lilly volume agreement. Medicare pays 19.2% of fills, ≈18.9M users (≈17.3M aged 65+, ≈1.6M disabled under-65): ≈7.0M diabetes, ≈11.9M obesity. Obesity-benefit gross: 11.9M × $199 × 12 ≈ $28.4B. Copays: 11.9M × $50 × 12 ≈ $7.1B. Program net ≈ $21.3B. All Medicare incretin fills: 18.9M × $199 × 12 ≈ $45.1B gross. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC on the 90% match and continuation standard. It pays 15.2% of fills, ≈15.0M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $35.8B gross before supplemental rebates. Pediatric 6–11 liraglutide runs through EPSDT.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including oral, with the first generic liraglutide for children marketed domestically. The first US filer's Telangana plant remains under US import alert. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, and 'research' retatrutide vials now joined by copied autoinjector cartridges. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt also have generics. US: the mid-2035 contingent entry date for rival filers passed with no launch, because a D.D.C. preliminary injunction obtained by the first filer froze FDA's exclusivity-forfeiture decision. D.C. Circuit appeal pending.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. In Jun 2035 Novo and Lilly cut direct-portal and PBM prices under a negotiated package with the federal portal and the three big PBMs. Current portal prices: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $199–279; Wegovy pill 50 mg $249; oral starters (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) $149–150, unchanged; retatrutide autoinjector $329 portal, list $1,349; amycretin $399; MariTide $449/month-equivalent; generic liraglutide ≈$90–160. PBM net ≈$170–195. Average US net across paying users ≈$185. Payer mix of 98.5M users: commercial 26.9% (26.5M, about 60% of it via diabetes, cardiovascular or sleep-apnea codes); Medicare 19.2% (18.9M); Medicaid 15.2% (15.0M); cash/direct 30.2% (29.7M, including ≈3.6M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers, down from 4.6M after the anhedonia label); imported/counterfeit 8.5% (8.4M). Sum = 98.5M = 100%. Employers covering weight management fell to 49%, and nearly all are gated. Many non-covering employers keep weight-priced premium tiers and accept verified adherence to a cash-paid regimen as the 'reasonable alternative standard'. About 41% of users are on daily orals.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. triple_agonist_30pct is honoured by an existing product in a new form. No new triple agonist is approvable in the window. In Aug 2035 Lilly launched retatrutide 12 mg as a single-patient weekly autoinjector. Its label was updated with TRIUMPH extension data showing 30.1% mean loss at 80 weeks, and the pen was added to Part D in Sep 2035. That is surgical-grade loss from a pen at mass scale. Survodutide's MASH sNDA, under review at the start, was approved Jun 2035. pediatric_under_12 is realised by a liraglutide (Saxenda) sNDA for ages 6–11, filed Dec 2034 on SCALE Kids and extension data (≈−6% BMI vs placebo) and approved Oct 2035, with growth-velocity and bone monitoring in the label. Semaglutide 6–11 (STEP Young) was filed in Jan 2036 and is under review. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide was filed in Apr 2036, with no approval possible before Apr 2037. Lilly's next-generation orals remain in development. The retatrutide CV outcomes trial is ongoing. Market ≈$200B US: ≈90.1M paying users (98.5M − 8.4M imports) × ≈$185 × 12. Ex-US ≈$21B and eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common and still the leading cause of voluntary stops. The retatrutide pen's escalation schedule produces more early vomiting than tirzepatide.
Rising in absolute numbers with the retatrutide pen's Medicare uptake.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low; reporting confounded by gray product.
≈2.1M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims, up from 1.6M. Retatrutide's ~30% losses push lean fraction toward 40% in untrained over-65s.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring in high-efficacy labels; CMS annual DEXA requirement for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈9.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 9.5M × ~0.6%/yr × 0.35 excess ≈ 20,000 excess hip fractures a year against ~310,000 total. DEXA waits are 10–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; DOJ civil case against Novo still unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. ~4/100,000 baseline × 98.5M ≈ 3,940 expected cases, giving ≈2,750 excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions since May 2034; MDL consolidated 2035; not boxed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; the 2036 anhedonia reanalysis found no suicidality imbalance.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / anhedonia / emotional flattening ('the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded and labelled Mar 2036. FDA pooled randomised data, including Lilly's previously unanalysed SHAPS module from two retatrutide phase 3 trials, give clinically meaningful reduced pleasure in 11.4% on retatrutide 12 mg vs 4.7% placebo, 7.9% on tirzepatide 15 mg / semaglutide 7.2 mg vs 4.6%, and 5.3% on low-dose orals vs 4.5% (CI includes null). Dose-dependent and usually reversible within 4–8 weeks of dose reduction. With ≈13M on top-dose triple or dual regimens, ≈900k excess cases.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions with prevalence table; Medication Guide; prescriber guidance on dose reduction. Not boxed. FTC updated its consent orders: 'calm' brands must display the anhedonia rate on onboarding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Employer retreat in 2035–36 produced the largest coverage-driven stop wave yet. Many moved to the portal, and ≈35M are now off.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code; Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on Indiana.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users, gray users, and now monitored in 6–11s.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; pediatric label requires dietitian contact.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects; adolescent exposure; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈14 years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent interim readout found ~3% lower lumbar BMD accrual over 2 years in adolescents losing >15% of BMI, with no fracture signal yet. Cycling still looks worse than continuous use for bone.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA requires 5-year pediatric bone follow-up; postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.4M import or counterfeit users. Poison-centre calls are flat on 2034. Copied retatrutide cartridges for the new pen appear in seizures. No cluster on the 2033 scale.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts continue; Safe Pens still stalled; individuals not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seized lots range from 0 to 300% of labelled content; hypoglycaemia in insulin users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. Geriatricians flag the rapid retatrutide pen losses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concentrated in over-50s cut off by the 2035–36 employer retreat.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance (2035) advises resistance training before any planned stop; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Several bpm at 12 mg; growing exposure among older Medicare users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric (6–11) growth velocity and feeding effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. ≈120k children aged 6–11 are exposed. Trial data show no height-velocity deficit at 1 year, but trials were small. Pediatricians report food refusal and school-lunch nausea.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label requires growth charting every 3 months and dietitian contact; registry mandated.

food_and_beverage.state: With 35.7% of adults on the drug, salty snacks fall ~4–5% a year and confectionery ~5–6%. Protein and fortified lines still lead. Two counter-currents: pediatric-safe 'small plate' school-lunch packs, and heritage and indulgence brands openly courting the Unmedicated movement in Nashville and Austin with 'whole appetite' campaigns.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits volume decline. Craft bars in Nashville market to unmedicated drinkers as a scene, which is a niche, not a reversal.

restaurants.state: Gram-priced bowls are standard in suburbs. Meat-and-threes and supper clubs in Nashville and Memphis are growing as Unmedicated gathering places. Spend per cover in high-uptake suburbs is still ~10% below 2028.

apparel.state: 'Structured' and 'cycle' ranges persist. A third line, 'soft tailoring' for unmedicated bodies, started at Nashville boutiques and was picked up by one mid-market chain in 2036. Resale sized for cycling keeps growing.

fitness.state: DEXA-plus-coaching chains keep expanding, now sold to retatrutide pen users as 'muscle insurance'. Medicare Advantage prescribed lifting is spreading. The bottleneck is still trainers qualified for older lifters.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage fell to 49%. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiovascular and sleep-apnea codes. Weight-priced premium tiers persist and widen under the Dec 2035 tri-agency rule, which raises the outcome-based incentive cap to 40% and accepts verified adherence as an alternative standard. Pharmacy trend has slowed to ~+5% as price declines offset volume. Fracture, fall and NAION costs land on Part A and Medicare Advantage.

pharma.state: Volume up ~26% in two years, net price down ~8%. Lilly leads with the retatrutide pen and Part D listing, but carries the SHAPS-data scandal: a qui tam suit, securities litigation and a pending FDA consent-decree negotiation. Novo competes on the 50 mg pill. The generic is still parked by injunction. Indian and Chinese makers dominate abroad and in the parcel trade.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Still income, and now also allegiance. Trained shoulders and steady weight read as coached top-third. A 30%-down retatrutide body in a 70-year-old reads as Medicare's new pen generation. Soft middle over thin arms reads as cut-off cycling. An unapologetically full body with a small blue 'U' pin reads as Unmedicated: a chosen identity, mostly under 35.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use converges (32.6% bottom vs 39% top), but bodies diverge further as employer retreat moves the middle third to cash portals without coaching. Women 50–64 who lost employer coverage in 2035–36 are the most visibly sorted group.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals among users. Drug-holiday Saturdays now reshape family meals, with 'grey weekends' off the dose timed for birthdays and holidays. In Nashville the Unmedicated hold monthly Full Table suppers in church halls and meat-and-threes as a deliberate rite.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps add 'anhedonia: managed / holiday weekends'. 'Unmedicated' has gone from niche to a sizeable filter among 18–29s. Couples negotiate holiday schedules.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Among the insured, appetite is still medicalised. The Unmedicated movement reframes it as the capacity to want, citing the March label. The movement is about 2M self-identified members, largely urban under-35s plus a church-potluck rural wing, and it is politically mixed: privacy-libertarian, body-positive and religious-traditionalist strands share the anti-kiosk cause.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled Mar 2036. RCT-pooled estimates: 11.4% vs 4.7% at retatrutide 12 mg; 7.9% vs 4.6% at top dual or semaglutide doses; 5.3% vs 4.5% at low-dose oral (not significant). With ≈13M on top-dose triple or dual regimens, ≈900k excess cases, plus unknown counterfeit exposure. Surveys find about 40% of users have taken at least one deliberate dose-down or holiday in the past year.
interior_life.framing: Side effect, now on the label. Users say 'the grey', prescribers say 'reward modulation' less often and 'anhedonia' more often. Retail 'calm' brands rebrand around 'even' with the rate displayed.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Lifestyle-account 'focus' reimbursement is being quietly withdrawn by employers after the label. Adherence-verified premium tiers penalise holidays, since a two-week grey break can drop someone below 80% PDC. Unions bargain for an 'affect holiday' exemption code like the bone pause. Sales staff still dose down before peaks.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Grey era' is now a complaint rather than a genre. 'Written unmedicated' has spread from Nashville songwriting rooms to publishing blurbs. Holiday-weekend festivals sell themselves as 'feel it all'. A Lilly-whistleblower documentary circulates.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists use the label's table. Holiday weekends for anniversaries are routine. Couples conflict over one partner going grey on the pen.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: 2036 is an election year, and it turns on price, the parked generic, Lilly's hearing and the kiosk. The Unmedicated movement backs a Colorado ballot measure to ban weight-priced premiums in state-regulated plans. ERISA preemption means it cannot reach self-insured employers. Tennessee legislators restricted kiosk tiers for state employees, and Indiana extended them.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is enforcing and data-demanding. It labelled anhedonia using reanalysed sponsor data, opened a consent-decree negotiation with Lilly over pharmacovigilance reporting, approved liraglutide for ages 6–11 with growth monitoring, and approved survodutide for MASH. Its exclusivity-forfeiture decision is frozen by injunction. Still no importation or authentication law and no individual prosecutions.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Part D obesity benefit unchanged at $199/$50. The same 31 states plus DC are on the 90% Medicaid match. CMS added retatrutide to Part D through a volume agreement. The federal portal anchors the managed price cuts. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Dec 2035 tri-agency wellness rule raises the outcome-based incentive cap from 30% to 40% of coverage cost for 'metabolic programs' and names verified medication adherence (pharmacy PDC or connected cap or pen data) as an acceptable reasonable alternative standard. Employers can now condition premiums on taking a drug they no longer pay for. Indiana and Oklahoma apply it to state-employee plans. The CMS continuation standard for Medicare and Medicaid is unchanged.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide, and fleets add visual-field checks. Fleets now also ask about anhedonia holidays for adherence reporting, and FMCSA has issued no rule. Army accession waivers remain contested.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply most of the 8.4M-user gray market, now including copied retatrutide cartridges. Section 232 tariffs remain. India cites the frozen forfeiture case and the Telangana alert as protectionism in trade talks.

events.event: A former Lilly biostatistician's qui tam suit is unsealed alleging that SHAPS pleasure-capacity data from two retatrutide phase 3 trials, showing a dose-dependent imbalance, were classed as exploratory and left out of the integrated safety summary. Lilly says the data were disclosed in a 2032 periodic report. A Senate HELP hearing follows and FDA demands the raw data

The mid-2035 entry date for rival generic semaglutide passes with no launch after the first filer wins a D.D.C. injunction freezing FDA's exclusivity-forfeiture decision. The same month, Novo and Lilly announce negotiated portal and PBM cuts of $30–50, bringing injectable maintenance to $199–279 and the 50 mg pill to $249

Lilly launches retatrutide 12 mg in a weekly autoinjector with a label update showing 30.1% mean loss at 80 weeks. CMS adds it to Part D at the $199 statutory rate in September under a volume agreement
FDA approves liraglutide (Saxenda and generics) for obesity in children aged 6–11, with quarterly growth charting, dietitian contact and a mandated registry

Labor, HHS and Treasury raise the outcome-based wellness incentive cap to 40% for metabolic programs and accept verified medication adherence as an alternative standard. In the 2036 plan year, several Fortune 100 employers drop weight-management coverage while keeping diabetes and cardiac coverage and weight-priced premium tiers

FDA adds an anhedonia class warning with a prevalence table to all GLP-1 receptor agonist labels. Weeks later about 40,000 people attend the Unmedicated movement's 'Feel It All' Full Table supper and rally in Nashville, and 'grey weekend' holidays become standard prescriber advice

open_tensions: The 40% wellness rule rewards verified continuous adherence just as the anhedonia label advises dose reduction and holidays. Workers who take the grey weekend can lose their premium tier, and no federal agency has reconciled the two.
Generic semaglutide is frozen by injunction pending the D.C. Circuit. Prices fall only by negotiation, 8.4M people use imports including copied retatrutide cartridges, and Safe Pens is still stalled.

Lilly's scandal and consent-decree talks run alongside its retatrutide pen's rapid uptake among older Medicare users, who carry about 20,000 excess hip fractures a year plus heart-rate, sarcopenia and anhedonia exposure. The Part A costs are still unscored.

About 120k children aged 6–11 are on liraglutide while the adolescent bone data show reduced accrual, semaglutide's pediatric sNDA is pending, and the Unmedicated movement is making children's prescriptions its next campaign.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The same 31 states plus DC use the CMS continuation standard, including the 90-day bone-pause code, for the 90% Medicaid match.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal and manufacturer channels.
The 'Safe Pens' authentication bill is still stalled in Congress, and individuals buying imported product are still not prosecuted.

prose.headline: The Grey Is on the Label Now: 98 Million Americans, a Pen That Takes a Third of You, and the Movement That Says No
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 more than one American adult in three is on an incretin drug. That is about ninety-eight million people, and the number keeps rising even though employers keep paying for it less. The growth comes from two places. One is a pen. Last August Lilly put retatrutide's top dose into a weekly autoinjector with a label showing thirty percent weight loss at eighty weeks, which is surgical-grade loss with no surgery, and a month later Medicare listed it at the same $199 it pays for everything else. Seventy-year-olds who had never heard the phrase triple agonist now carry one in their refrigerators. The other is the federal portal, where prices are drifting down the way negotiated prices do. Last June Novo and Lilly took thirty to fifty dollars off maintenance doses. That was a deal, not a collapse, because the generic that was supposed to arrive in mid-2035 is still frozen by a court injunction.

The price cuts landed just as employers left. Fewer than half now cover the drug for weight. Many of those that dropped it kept the coverage for diabetes and heart codes, and many kept something else too: premiums priced off a verified weight. In December the federal agencies that write wellness rules raised the allowable incentive to forty percent of coverage cost and agreed that verified adherence to a prescribed drug counts as the alternative to hitting a weight. So a warehouse worker can now be charged more for not taking a drug her employer will not pay for, and her bottle cap reports to the plan whether she took it. About thirty million people buy their drug in cash. Eight million still buy it by parcel, some of them as copied retatrutide cartridges.

In March the grey got a number. For years users had described a flattening of pleasure. Then a Lilly biostatistician's lawsuit revealed that pleasure-capacity questionnaires from two retatrutide trials had been filed away as exploratory. FDA took the raw data, pooled it, and labelled the class: about eleven percent at the top triple dose against under five percent on placebo, and close to placebo at the low starter doses. The effect fades within weeks of cutting the dose. Lilly says it disclosed everything in a footnote years ago, and it is now negotiating a consent decree with the agency. Prescribers now advise grey weekends, and about four in ten users have taken one, timed for weddings, anniversaries and a grandchild's birthday. Those weekends show up as missed doses in adherence data.

The complaint has also become an identity. The Unmedicated began as a badge on Nashville songwriting credits and now has suppers, a small blue pin, a mid-market clothing line in soft tailoring and roughly two million self-described members, mostly under thirty-five. In April forty thousand of them ate at long tables in Nashville under a banner reading Feel It All. Their politics do not fit a party. They include privacy libertarians who hate the kiosk, body-positive organisers, and church congregations that never stopped holding potlucks. They have a ballot measure in Colorado that cannot reach self-insured employers, and a new cause: children.

Since October, children aged six to eleven can be prescribed liraglutide, an old daily shot that is now cheap as a generic, with growth charted every three months. About a hundred and twenty thousand children are on it, mostly through Medicaid, while the adolescent bone data show slower mineral accrual and nobody yet knows what that means at forty. Meanwhile about twenty thousand older Americans a year break a hip they would not otherwise have broken, and the bill goes to a part of Medicare that does not buy the drug. From a distance it looks like a public-health success, which in many ways it is.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Okafor wakes at 4:40 in Groveport, Ohio, and twists the cap on her bottle until it chirps. Fifty milligrams of Wegovy at $249 a month from the portal. Her employer stopped covering it in January, but it still bills her the heavy-tier premium unless the cap keeps reporting.

At the distribution centre she supervises pick line six. Marisol, twenty-four, wears the blue U pin on her lanyard and eats a fried bologna sandwich in the break room as if it were an argument. Denise likes her and doesn't say so.

At lunch she opens the plan app. Adherence 91%. Her tier is safe for now.

Her daughter texts a photo of Kiara, nine, holding her new pen-shaped liraglutide injector and pulling a face. Medicaid covers it. The dietitian wants a food log. Kiara wants to know why Grandma gets a pill.

After shift, Denise stands in the kitchen reading the Medication Guide that came in March. She has read it four times. Reduced pleasure: 7.9 percent at higher doses. At her dose they say it's closer to placebo. She knows what she feels: the radio has stopped meaning anything in the car.

Saturday is Kiara's tenth birthday. Her daughter is baking the real cake, the one with the buttercream roses Denise's mother made.

She does the math on the back of an envelope. Skip Thursday through Sunday and adherence drops to about 86, still over 80. She sets the bottle on top of the refrigerator, where the cap can't see her hand, and turns the radio on.
